title: Structural Adaptations
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Structural Adaptations Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Examine how particular structural features and behaviours of living things enable their survival in specific habitats (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on structural adaptations: how the body parts of Australian animals and plants help them survive in deserts, rainforests, oceans and mangroves. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Structural adaptations are features a living thing is born with.
body_html:
How to think about it

A structural adaptation is a body part that helps a living thing survive.

  • Look at the habitat first: is it hot, dry, cold, wet, salty or dark?
  • Then match the feature: a thorny devil's grooved skin collects water; a koala's two thumbs grip branches; banksia pods open after fire.
  • Behavioural adaptations are things a living thing does, such as coming out at night.
Example

Bilby with large ears in the desert. Why?

the desert is hot

ears lose heat and hear predators

Answer: keeps cool, hears danger

Example

Spiky, rolled-up leaves. Habitat?

small leaf area loses less water

Answer: hot, dry desert

Common mistakes

  • Saying an animal grows a feature because it needs it.
  • Mixing up structural features (body parts) and behaviours (actions).
  • Thinking every feature is for keeping warm.

faq.q: What is the difference between a structural and a behavioural adaptation?
faq.a: A structural adaptation is a body part, such as a kangaroo's tail. A behavioural adaptation is something a living thing does, such as a bilby coming out at night.
Many have small, spiky or waxy leaves that lose less water, deep or spreading roots to collect water, and stems that store water.

faq.q: Why do Australian animals have such different features?
faq.a: They live in many habitats, from deserts to rainforests and reefs. Over a long time, living things with features that suit their habitat survive and reproduce.

items.q: How do the woody pods of banksias help them survive bushfires?
